headline: NEWMONT'S CADIA HALTED AGAIN — TWIN EARTHQUAKES FREEZE AUSTRALIA'S BIGGEST GOLD MINE FOR SECOND TIME IN NINE WEEKS
snippet: Underground operations at Newmont's Cadia gold-copper mine in New South Wales, Australia — 11% of Newmont's net asset value and one of the world's largest gold mines — were suspended on June 19, 2026 after two earthquakes struck the site: a magnitude-3.2 tremor at approximately 3:20 a.m. local time followed by a magnitude-3.4 event at approximately 5:45 a.m. All underground personnel were safely returned to the surface with no injuries reported. The June 19 halt is the second seismic disruption in nine weeks: an April 14 magnitude-4.5 earthquake caused a suspension from which Newmont only recently completed its five-week recovery plan, restoring approximately 80% of capacity. Cadia produced approximately 385,000 ounces of gold and 82,000 tonnes of copper in 2025, making it a globally significant supply source for both metals — copper at a moment when the June 30 US copper tariff decision looms, and gold in a week when the market was already watching Alamos Gold's Young-Davidson seismic events. The second major seismic halt at Cadia in nine weeks introduces meaningful supply uncertainty into Newmont's H1 production outlook, with full normalization now delayed beyond the third quarter. For investors tracking gold producer operating risk, Cadia's repeat seismic vulnerability — a known geomechanical characteristic of deep block-cave mining environments — illustrates that even the most technically sophisticated operations can face repeated disruptions from geology rather than operator error.

headline: ABRASILVER FILES 454 MOZ AGEQ TECHNICAL REPORT ON DIABLILLOS — SALTA SILVER DEPOSIT GROWS 30% TO 248 MOZ Ag + 2.54 MOZ Au IN M&I
source_name: Newsfile Corp. / AbraSilver Resource Corp. (TSX: ABRA)
snippet: AbraSilver Resource Corp. (TSX: ABRA) filed its NI 43-101 Technical Report on June 19, 2026, formally completing the disclosure package for an updated Mineral Resource Estimate at the Diablillos silver-gold project in Salta Province, Argentina — with effective date May 6, 2026. The Measured and Indicated resource stands at 232 million tonnes containing 248 million ounces of silver and 2.54 million ounces of gold, or approximately 454 million ounces silver-equivalent — representing a 25% increase in silver and 48% increase in gold versus the prior July 2025 estimate, incorporating approximately 13,270 metres of additional drilling to a total database exceeding 170,000 metres. At current spot prices of approximately $65/oz silver and $4,350/oz gold, the M&I resource contains approximately $16.1 billion of silver and $11.1 billion of gold at spot — making Diablillos one of the largest undeveloped silver-gold resources in the Americas. The Definitive Feasibility Study was on track for Q2 2026 completion, and the Province of Salta granted the principal Environmental Impact Assessment approval in April 2026 — the two milestones required before construction permitting can begin. For silver mining investors navigating the current $65/oz silver market following the January $121 ATH correction, a 454 Moz AgEq technical report filing confirms Diablillos as a globally significant deposit advancing through feasibility in one of South America's most accessible mining corridors, at a scale that attracts senior producer M&A interest at current silver prices.

headline: STLLR GOLD HITS 13.00 g/t Au OVER 22.75m AT JONPOL — TIMMINS TOWER PROJECT ADDS TO STREAK OF WIDE HIGH-GRADE ONTARIO INTERCEPTS
source_name: Junior Mining Network / STLLR Gold Inc. (TSX: STLR)
snippet: STLLR Gold Inc. (TSX: STLR) reported June 18, 2026 additional assay results from its 2026 drilling program at the Jonpol Deposit on the Garrison Property of the Tower Gold Project in Ontario's Timmins Mining Camp. Standout intercepts include 13.00 g/t Au (uncut) over 22.75 metres from hole MGA26-266, and 3.01 g/t Au over 22.93 metres from the same program release — alongside hole MGA26-265 returning 10.10 g/t Au over 5.57 metres and 2.55 g/t Au over 19.70 metres (including 20.22 g/t Au over 1.84 metres), and hole MGA26-264 intersecting 2.07 g/t Au over 19.00 metres. The company has completed 8,536 metres for the first-half 2026 drill program at Jonpol with assay results pending for remaining holes. Jonpol is a high-grade gold deposit within the broader Tower Gold Project, a large-scale multi-deposit gold system in the prolific Timmins district of Ontario — home to some of the world's most productive underground gold mines. Wide, high-grade intercepts at depth in a Timmins-district deposit are the data signature that historically supports PEA and resource expansion scenarios, and consistent multi-hole releases maintaining both grade and width demonstrate geological continuity rather than isolated pods of mineralization — the most important deliverable in an underground development-stage drilling program.

headline: MERCADO MINERALS HITS 1,120 g/t AgEq IN 1.2m AT COPALITO — SINALOA HIGH-SULPHIDATION VEIN OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS FROM FIRST-EVER DRILL
source_name: Newsfile Corp. / Mercado Minerals Ltd. (CSE: MERC; OTCQB: MRMNF)
snippet: Mercado Minerals Ltd. (CSE: MERC) reported June 18, 2026 drill results from its inaugural 3,000-metre diamond drill program at the Copalito Project in Sinaloa, Mexico — intersecting 1.20 metres grading 1,120 g/t silver equivalent (34 g/t Ag, 3.40 g/t Au, 19.00% Pb, 21.00% Zn) from 124.75 metres depth at the El Agua vein, within a broader 3.50-metre interval at 686 g/t AgEq. The El Agua hole successfully targeted a new, steeper-dipping structural interpretation of the vein, and mineralization remains open in all directions — providing a new expansion centre for follow-up drilling. At the 5 Señores Vein, drilling expanded the productive strike length to approximately 800 metres and defined 125 metres of vertical depth, also identifying a fault offset extension to the southeast with a separate 250-metre strike corridor. Sinaloa's Fresnillo belt and adjacent vein districts are among the world's most prolific silver-base metal epithermal environments; the combination of 1,120 g/t AgEq vein grades with multi-component base metal credits (lead-zinc) at shallow depths in an inaugural drill program is the signature that defines the polymetallic vein systems most sought by junior silver mining investors — high-grade core with open geometry on multiple fronts from day one.

headline: BRIXTON METALS TARGETS MAIDEN TAILINGS MRE AT COBALT SILVER CAMP — HISTORIC 20-25 OPT MATERIAL DRILLED FOR NEAR-TERM CASH FLOW
snippet: Brixton Metals Corporation (TSXV: BBB) announced June 18, 2026 the commencement of a dedicated sonic-drilling campaign to define a potential maiden Mineral Resource Estimate from historic tailings at its Langis Silver Project in the Cobalt silver mining camp of Ontario, Canada. Historical processing data from the 1956–1968 period references average feed grades of approximately 20 to 25 ounces per ton silver with potential recoveries of approximately 88% — grades that represent legacy inefficiency from mid-20th century metallurgical methods, and the source of significant silver value potentially recoverable with modern processing. The tailings program runs alongside two bedrock rigs executing Brixton's fully funded 60,000-metre 2026 exploration program, bringing the total active rig count to three across the Langis property. Ontario's Recovery of Minerals regime, enacted July 1, 2025, created a streamlined permitting pathway — a recovery permit rather than a full closure plan — that materially reduces the regulatory burden for qualifying tailings recovery projects. For retail silver investors, Cobalt-district tailings programs occupy a distinct position in the junior silver ecosystem: they offer defined, surface-accessible material with documented historical grades, near-term permitting optionality under new Ontario regulations, and the potential for cash-flow generation that could partially fund ongoing bedrock exploration — a self-funding exploration loop that is rare among early-stage silver juniors.

headline: PUREPOINT-ISOENERGY JV OPENS SUMMER DRILL AT DORADO'S NOVA — 7 HOLES TARGET 1KM ATHABASCA HIGH-GRADE URANIUM CORRIDOR
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Purepoint Uranium Group Inc. (TSXV: PTU) + IsoEnergy Ltd.
snippet: Purepoint Uranium Group Inc. (TSXV: PTU) and IsoEnergy Ltd. announced the commencement of the summer 2026 drill program at the Dorado Project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — a 50/50 joint venture covering more than 98,000 hectares of eastern Athabasca exploration ground. The seven-hole, approximately 3,150-metre summer program runs through July and August 2026, targeting expansion of the Nova uranium discovery on a one-kilometre structural corridor where winter 2026 drilling confirmed high-grade mineralization including 8.1% U3O8 over 0.4 metres within 2.1 metres at 1.6% U3O8. Winter drilling successfully expanded Nova across the full kilometre of structural corridor and refined the geological model; the summer program is designed to step out systematically from the winter holes to establish downdip and along-strike continuity. The Athabasca Basin hosts the world's highest-grade uranium deposits — Cameco's McArthur River and Cigar Lake, among others — and basement-hosted discoveries like Nova follow the structural corridor model that defines the basin's most significant historical discoveries. With uranium spot at approximately $86/lb and US utilities structurally under-contracted through the early 2030s, a summer drill program on a high-grade basement-hosted discovery in the most productive uranium jurisdiction on earth is among the highest-leverage exploration programs available in the uranium sector in 2026.

headline: ENERGY FUELS ON TRACK FOR FULL-YEAR URANIUM GUIDANCE BY MID-2026 — WHITE MESA MILL PROCESSING CAMPAIGN WRAPS END OF JUNE
source_name: PR Newswire / Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU) announced it expects to complete the current uranium ore processing campaign at its White Mesa Mill in Utah by the end of June 2026, rebuilding ore stockpiles following a successful conventional mining campaign across its network of licensed uranium mines. The Company expects to resume ore processing at the Mill in Q4-2026, subject to continued strong ore production at conventional mines, uranium market conditions, and the potential for a rare earth element processing campaign in the interim period. The mid-year production guidance achievement is a separate operational milestone from the company's ongoing merger with Australian Strategic Materials (ASX: ASM), whose shareholder vote was postponed from June 22 to accommodate new disclosure requirements triggered by the U.S. Pentagon's conditional loan commitment to the combined entity. For uranium investors, the White Mesa Mill's processing schedule — completing the 2026 ore campaign on time at the midpoint of the year — demonstrates that Energy Fuels' existing uranium production infrastructure is performing to plan even as the company simultaneously pursues the largest strategic transaction in its history. White Mesa is the only operating conventional uranium and vanadium mill in the United States and, pending ASM merger completion, the only operating uranium-to-rare-earth solvent extraction facility on the continent.

headline: G2 GOLDFIELDS SHAREHOLDERS APPROVE G MINING DEAL — GUYANA GOLD HUB SET TO CLOSE BY JULY WITH C$1B+ IN SYNERGIES
source_name: Junior Mining Network / G2 Goldfields Inc. (TSX: GTWO) + G Mining Ventures Corp. (TSX: GMIN)
snippet: G2 Goldfields Inc. (TSX: GTWO) shareholders voted on June 16, 2026 to approve the plan of arrangement under which G Mining Ventures Corp. (TSX: GMIN) acquires all of G2's outstanding shares — clearing the key shareholder condition for a transaction the companies describe as uniquely synergistic due to the direct adjacency of G2's Oko-Ghanie Project and GMIN's fully permitted, fully financed Oko West Project in Guyana. Under the terms, G2 shareholders receive 0.212 GMIN shares plus 0.5 shares of G3 Goldfields (a spin-out entity retaining G2's earlier-stage assets) per G2 share held, at an implied 72% premium to the undisturbed price at announcement. Completion is targeted for early July 2026, subject to final court approval and standard regulatory conditions. The combined entity is projected to realize over C$1 billion in quantifiable synergies through shared infrastructure, mine sequencing, and permitting across the adjacent projects — creating one of the lowest-cost large-scale gold operations in the Americas in a single Guyanese mining district. For investors watching Guyana as an emerging Latin American gold jurisdiction — following ExxonMobil's oil development transforming Guyana's fiscal capacity and infrastructure — the GMIN/G2 consolidation is the defining corporate transaction that crystallizes the Oko district's potential as a Tier-One gold mining hub under a proven operating team.

headline: RECORD Q1, RISING Q2 COSTS: FUEL SHOCKS THREATEN GOLD MINER MARGINS JUST AS GOLD PRICE PULLS BACK 25% FROM THE HIGH
snippet: Crux Investor published a mid-June 2026 analysis identifying the structural tension now facing gold mining equities: Q1 2026 marked peak earnings for the sector at an average realized gold price of approximately $4,900 per ounce, with major producers reporting record revenues, EBITDA, and free cash flow simultaneously — but Q2 faces a double compression from the approximately $200/oz gold price decline from January's all-time high and a 50–100% spike in refined fuel costs across key mining jurisdictions. Diesel accounts for 15–25% of all-in sustaining costs for open-pit operations; at sustained oil prices in the $90–100 range, sector-wide AISC could increase 5–9% above original 2026 guidance — with consumables inflation typically lagging crude oil by one to two quarters, reinforcing H2 2026 as the key margin pressure window rather than Q2 alone. Australia is identified as the most fuel-exposed major mining jurisdiction (importing 91% of refined products), while underground, grid-connected mines face relatively contained exposure of 4–5% of cost structure. For retail investors assessing gold producer equity valuations following the correction from $5,589 to current ~$4,350 gold, the cost-side analysis provides a critical offset to the gold price bull case: the margin expansion that drove junior-to-senior producer equity re-rating through Q1 2026 may not persist into Q3-Q4 even if gold stabilizes — making corporate cost discipline, geographic diversification away from fuel-import-dependent jurisdictions, and underground versus open-pit operational mix the new screening variables in a market where revenue per ounce has declined but cost per ounce is rising.

headline: SILVER'S SIXTH CONSECUTIVE ANNUAL DEFICIT DEEPENS — CHINA EXPORT CONTROLS RESTRICT 60-70% OF GLOBAL SUPPLY AS COMEX INVENTORY SINKS 70% FROM 2020
source_name: GoldSeek (Silver Institute 2026 World Silver Survey Data / China Export Licensing Framework)
snippet: The silver market is entering its sixth consecutive annual structural deficit in 2026, with the Silver Institute projecting a shortfall of approximately 200–230 million ounces — the largest in the current deficit cycle — driven by the collision of two simultaneous forces: persistent industrial demand growth from solar, defence electronics, and EV applications, and China's January 2026 export licensing framework that effectively restricts 60–70% of global silver export capacity by requiring annual production floors of at least 80 tonnes and credit lines exceeding $30 million for license eligibility, excluding the majority of mid-sized export firms. China imported 790-plus tonnes of silver in early 2026 while simultaneously tightening outbound flows — a supply squeeze from the world's largest silver processing nation that the COMEX is directly reflecting: US commercial exchange inventories have declined approximately 70% since 2020. The current $64–65 per ounce silver price — down from January's $121 all-time high — creates an unusual divergence: the speculative premium has been eliminated by the FOMC hawkish hold and the Iran conflict's dollar strength, but the structural industrial deficit has not changed in direction. For junior silver mining investors, the sixth-consecutive-deficit structure combined with China's export restrictions provides the fundamental demand floor under which speculative positioning corrections occur — not reversals. The same deficit that drove silver's $121 January ATH is running on unchanged underlying demand growth; only the speculative overlay has been removed.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE SOFTENS TO TWO-MONTH LOW AS AUSSIE MINE RESTARTS REBUILD SUPPLY — BALD HILL AND FINNISS RE-ENTER MARKET
source_name: Trading Economics / MINING.COM (Mineral Resources; Core Lithium)
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate in China fell to approximately CNY 163,000 per tonne (roughly US$22,500/t) in mid-June 2026, the lowest level in nearly two months, as scheduled production restarts at Mineral Resources' Bald Hill lithium mine and Core Lithium's Finniss project re-entered the market and began rebuilding supply against an easing of the acute tightness that drove Q1 2026's near-doubling of carbonate prices to CNY 200,000 peak in mid-May. Despite the June correction, lithium carbonate remains approximately 177% higher year-over-year — reflecting the severity of the 2024–2025 bear market floor below CNY 80,000 per tonne that preceded the recovery. The Bald Hill and Finniss restarts represent Australian spodumene supply chain reconstitution: both mines were idled in 2024 due to low prices and are now re-opening into a market where the energy storage demand base — projected to grow approximately 55% in 2026, driven by data centres, utility-scale batteries, and industrial installations — is structurally larger than the supply base available at cycle trough. For junior lithium developers, the two-month price softening from the May peak is a natural demand-supply recalibration from a short-term supply squeeze, not a structural reversal: the Macquarie-forecast 20%-per-year demand growth trajectory through 2030 requires project pipelines that these price corrections do not justify abandoning.
